title: Leaks beyond Bits: Deep Learning-Assisted Side-Channel Attacks on Hyperdimensional Computing Accelerators
problem: FPGA-based Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) accelerators are vulnerable to side-channel attacks that can extract stored hypervector bits, compromising security of edge/IoT applications.
motivation: Understanding HDC side-channel vulnerabilities is essential for developing robust countermeasures in resource-constrained edge devices.
method: The approach uses a deep learning model (a convolutional neural network or CNN—a type of AI trained to find patterns in data) to detect side-channel leaks in FPGA-based hyperdimensional computing hardware, where side-channels are unintended physical signals like power consumption or electromagnetic emissions that reveal what data is being processed. It improves accuracy by using Grad-CAM (a technique that identifies which parts of the sensor data are most revealing), which iteratively pinpoints the measurement regions most useful for extracting the secret hypervector bits and strengthens the signal-to-noise ratio. The paper also introduces dynamic masking as a protective countermeasure against such attacks.
key_novelty: The core innovation is combining a neural network with automated attention mapping (Grad-CAM) to discover which physical signals are most useful for extracting secrets from hyperdimensional computing accelerators.
contributions: CNN-based side-channel analysis specialized for HDC accelerators
Adaptive Grad-CAM-guided approach improving leakage detection efficiency
93% bit extraction accuracy using ~1M power traces
Dynamic masking countermeasure reducing CNN extraction accuracy to ~18%
limitations: Evaluation limited to Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA; transferability to other platforms not addressed.
primary_theme: CNN-based side-channel attacks on HDC accelerators
